newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Wall Street unhinges European investors.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Wall Street unhinges European investors.

text.p: European investors took fright on Wednesday after watching the U.S. stock and bond markets soar then plunge overnight.

The strength of the dollar, trading below its session highs against the yen and mark, helped German stocks. But nerves spawned by Wall Street's gyrations clawed back Tuesday's gains on the London and Paris stock markets.

Although U.S. shares traded in London were steady to slightly higher in the morning, investors remained wary of another Wall Street slide. All eyes were fixed on U.S. durable goods data due at 1330 GMT.

U.S. blue chips rose more than 100 points after Tuesday's mild inflation news before profit-taking wiped out the gains and sent the Dow Jones industrial average to its fifth consecutive loss with a decline of 4.61 points.
Wall Street shadowed the volatile bond market which saw the Treasury's key 30-year security rally more than a full point before it lost steam.
"It was definitely a shock to see the Dow Jones ending lower after being up 100 points," one German dealer said.
In London, Sanwa International strategist Kirit Shah said: "Volatility is rising. I look for equities and bonds to remain weak."
On foreign exchange markets, the dollar hovered below fresh highs against the yen and mark but dealers said the upward trend remained intact.
By 1200 GMT the dollar was quoted at 1.6420 marks and 122.35 yen compared with late Tuesday's European level of 1.6496 marks and 121.31 yen.
The dollar's rise to a 47-month high against the yen in Asian trading provided the spark needed to push Tokyo stocks up more than three percent.

"The economy in the U.S. is looking very good, so the dollar has more of an upside in general...But I think we'll see the yen strengthening a bit today," said Glenn Davies, chief economist at Credit Lyonnais Laing in London.
In Europe, however, Wall Street's problems provided the major influence.
British shares slid in early trading, giving back Tuesday's gains after investor nerves were unhinged by New York.
"We've had another predictable mark down. The Dow falls and we have a poor open," the head of trading at large brokerage said.
As the FTSE 100 came off its lows to show a fall of 27 points to 4,209 by 1200 GMT, Shah warned: "If the Dow does have a major correction the FTSE could go down to 3,750 to 3,800."

Enterprise Oil, which jumped on Tuesday on news of an oil find in the Gulf of Mexico, rose another 10.5p to 652 after the company said it had completed a sucessful appraisal of an oil discovery in southern Italy.
French shares shed some of Tuesday's sharp gains in early trading, but traders said they were not too worried about the Paris market which later came off its lows.
The bourse needed a pause after recent strong advances, they said, and the continued strength of the dollar provided support.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was down 17 points, or 0.66 percent, at 2,465.
Oil company Total rose 0.8 percent to 478 francs after reporting 1996 earnings at the top end of analyst forecasts.

Following early sharp falls in German screen-based trading, the 30-share DAX index opened floor trading by catching up with Tuesday's late afternoon rally. Floor trade had closed before U.S. wage cost data was released.
Traders said they expected the market to remain range-bound through the day, although the dollar's strength was providing support.
CURRENCIES AT 1200 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.6420 marks and 122.35 yen compared with late Tuesday's European level of 1.6496 marks and 121.31 yen.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1200 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE 100 index of leading shares was down 27.8 points, or 0.66 percent, at 4,209.6.
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index was down 17.08 points, or 0.69 percent, at 2,465.68.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was up 16.67 points, or 0.56 percent, at 3,006.00.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $350.15 against $353.70. Silver was six cents weaker at $4.91.
